name: What happens if we find mold, rot, or old wiring during demolition?

mainEntity.name: What happens if mold, rot, or outdated wiring is found during kitchen demolition?
mainEntity.text: What happens if mold, rot, or outdated wiring is found during kitchen demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unexpected problems found during demolition usually stop or slow the remodel until the issue is evaluated and fixed. Older homes can hide mold, rot, termite damage, damaged subfloors, undersized electrical service, unsafe wiring, leaks, or previous unpermitted work. When that happens, the contractor should document the condition, explain the fix, and present a change order before additional work proceeds. In some cases, a specialist may need to be brought in for testing, remediation, or code-related repairs. This is one reason contingency funds matter on kitchen remodels, especially in older Los Angeles homes. Homeowners should ask in advance how hidden conditions are handled, who approves the repair scope, and whether the schedule will be adjusted. A good contractor will not rush over a safety issue just to keep moving. Addressing problems correctly protects the rest of the remodel and reduces the risk of future failures.
acceptedAnswer.description: Unexpected problems found during demolition usually require a change order, additional inspection, and extra repair work before the remodel can continue. Mold, rot, faulty plumbing, and outdated wiring are common hidden issues in older homes and should be covered in the project contingency.
